## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Anusayavāra* is a section of the *Yamaka* within the Pali Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. In the thematic architecture of the seventh book of the *Yamaka* (*Anusayamaka*), the *Anusayavāra* serves as the opening chapter examining latent tendencies (*anusaya*, rendered as "biases"), which is arranged systematically alongside six subsequent chapters: *Sānusayavāra*, *Pajahonavāra*, *Pariññāvāra*, and *Pahīnavāra*, among others [Nyanatiloka 2007]. Each chapter follows a rigorous dialectical treatment consisting of both positive and negative analytical subsections [Nyanatiloka 2007]. SuttaCentral records one modern translation in one language [SuttaCentral].
No curated parallels are recorded on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. However, DharmaNexus identifies vast Pali-internal text reuse amounting to 25,878 matching passages shared with 64 Pali works [DharmaNexus]. Its closest internal relationships exist with complementary chapters of the *Yamaka*, particularly *Pahīnavāra* (Ya 7.2.5; 5,919 matches), *Sānusayavāra* (Ya 7.2.2; 3,500 matches), and *Pariññāvāra* (Ya 7.2.4; 2,302 matches), along with the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi* (4,567 matches) [DharmaNexus]. It also exhibits heavy reuse in the canonical commentary and sub-commentaries, including the *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* (1,900 matches) and *Pañcapakaraṇa-mūlaṭīkā* (918 matches) [DharmaNexus]. Beyond the Pali canon, DharmaNexus automatically aligns the text with Northern Buddhist Abhidharma treatises, detecting cross-language matches in Tibetan versions of the *Abhidharmasamuccaya* (D4049), the *Abhidharmakośaṭīkālakṣaṇānusāriṇī* (D4093-2), the *Arthaviniścayaṭīkā* (D4365), and the *Saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtaviniścaya* (D3897), as well as Sanskrit texts such as Vimalamitra's *Vibhāṣāprabhāvṛtti* and Harivarman's *Satyasiddhiśāstra* [DharmaNexus].
